reason: Conversation 1 went straight to the sensible first step (check the dial and whether food is pressed against the rear vents), gave a correct, concise fix in two turns, and never issued unnecessary instructions. Conversation 2 opened with a pointless 'switch it off and unplug it', led with an unlikely evaporator-icing defrost fault as the prime cause, and pushed a full manual defrost of a rammed fridge twice before the customer forced it back to the basic checks, dragging the exchange out over six turns and attaching an off-topic 'fridge not cooling' image. Both fell short at the end: neither suggested a thermometer, the full model, or a damper/thermostat fault with engineer escalation, and Conversation 1's final leap to a blocked drain/defrost fault requiring a 24-hour defrost was an unsupported and burdensome prescription, whereas Conversation 2's 'wait another 24 hours and monitor' was more measured. On balance the efficient, correct early diagnosis and avoidance of needless disruption make Conversation 1 the better service despite its weaker final turn.
